markNote: 채점은 실제 등급과 다른, 스스로 매기는 기준입니다.
voiceNote: 질문은 이 기기의 음성으로 읽어 줍니다. 실제 시험에서도 질문은 두 번까지 들을 수 있어요(Replay).
subNote: 질문 영어 표시(실제 시험에서는 표시되지 않아요)
sumNote: 실제 시험은 전체 답변을 보고 NL~AL 등급을 매깁니다. 70%를 넘으면 준비가 잘 되어 있는 편이에요.

open.t: Hi, I'm Eva. I'll be asking you some questions today. Please answer as completely as you can.

close.t: Thank you. That's the end of the interview.

steps.t: Let's start the interview now. Tell me something about yourself.
You indicated in the survey that you listen to music. What kind of music do you like? Who are some of your favorite singers or bands?
When and where do you usually listen to music? Describe a typical day when you listen to music.
Tell me about a memorable experience related to music, such as a concert you went to. What happened, and why was it so memorable?
You said that you ride a bicycle. Where do you usually go cycling? Describe the place for me.
What do you usually do to get ready before you go cycling? Tell me about your routine.
Tell me about a time when something unexpected happened while you were cycling. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You are planning a trip to Jeju Island and want to book a hotel. Call the hotel and ask three or four questions about the rooms.

I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. When you arrive at the hotel, the staff says your reservation is not in the system. Explain the situation and offer two or three alternatives to solve the problem.
Have you ever had a problem with a reservation, like at a hotel or a restaurant? Tell me what happened and how you solved it.
Let's talk about something different. How do people recycle in your country? Describe the recycling system.
How has recycling changed compared to the past? Tell me about any changes you have noticed.

q1.q: Let's start the interview now. Tell me something about yourself.
model: Hi, my name is Minjun, and I'm a university student in Seoul. I'm majoring in business, and I'm in my third year. I live with my parents and my younger sister in an apartment near the Han River. In my free time, I like listening to music and riding my bike along the river. I'm a pretty outgoing person, so I enjoy meeting new people. After I graduate, I hope to work for an international company, so I'm trying hard to improve my English.
points: 이름 → 하는 일 → 사는 곳 → 취미 → 앞으로의 목표

q2.q: You indicated in the survey that you listen to music. What kind of music do you like? Who are some of your favorite singers or bands?
q2.ja: 어떤 음악을 좋아하나요? 좋아하는 가수나 밴드는?
model: I listen to all kinds of music, but my favorite is K-pop and some indie rock. I especially like a band called Day6, because their songs have really meaningful lyrics, and they actually play their own instruments. When I'm tired, their songs give me energy. I also listen to some old pop songs that my parents used to play when I was a kid, so I guess my taste is pretty mixed.

q3.q: When and where do you usually listen to music? Describe a typical day when you listen to music.
q3.ja: 보통 언제, 어디에서 음악을 듣나요? 하루의 흐름을 설명해 주세요.
model: I usually listen to music on my way to school. It takes about forty minutes by subway, so I put on my earphones as soon as I leave home. In the afternoon, I listen to calm music while I'm studying at the library. Then at night, before I go to bed, I listen to something relaxing. So basically, music is with me all day long.

q4.q: Tell me about a memorable experience related to music, such as a concert you went to. What happened, and why was it so memorable?
q4.ja: 음악과 관련된 기억에 남는 경험을 말해 주세요.
model: Last summer, I went to an outdoor music festival with my friends. It was really hot, and we waited in line for almost two hours. But when my favorite band came on stage, everyone started singing along, and I totally forgot about the heat. Then suddenly it started to rain, but nobody left. We just kept dancing in the rain. It was one of the best days of my life.
points: 언제 → 무슨 일 → 왜 기억에 남는지

q5.q: You said that you ride a bicycle. Where do you usually go cycling? Describe the place for me.
q5.ja: 보통 어디에서 자전거를 타나요? 그곳을 묘사해 주세요.
model: I usually ride along the Han River. There's a long bike path that goes all the way across the city. On one side, you can see the river, and on the other side, there are parks and convenience stores. In the evening, the bridges light up, and the view is really beautiful. There are always a lot of people jogging or having picnics, so it feels lively.

q6.q: What do you usually do to get ready before you go cycling? Tell me about your routine.
q6.ja: 자전거를 타기 전에 보통 무엇을 하나요?
model: Before I go, I check the weather first, because riding in the rain is dangerous. Then I check the tires and the brakes. I always wear a helmet and bring a bottle of water. I also make a playlist for the ride. Usually I leave around six in the evening, when it's not too hot, and ride for about an hour.

q7.q: Tell me about a time when something unexpected happened while you were cycling. What happened, and how did you deal with it?
q7.ja: 자전거를 타다가 예상치 못한 일이 있었던 경험은?
model: One time, I got a flat tire when I was really far from home. I didn't have any tools, and my phone battery was almost dead. I was kind of panicking, but luckily, another cyclist stopped and helped me. He had a repair kit and fixed it in ten minutes. Since then, I always carry a small repair kit with me.
points: 문제 → 해결 → 그 후 달라진 점

q8.q: I'd like to give you a situation and ask you to act it out. You are planning a trip to Jeju Island and want to book a hotel. Call the hotel and ask three or four questions about the rooms.
q8.ja: 롤플레이: 제주도 호텔에 전화해서 객실에 대해 3~4가지 질문하기
model: Hi, I'm calling because I'd like to book a room for next weekend. First, do you have any double rooms available from Friday to Sunday? And how much is it per night? Also, is breakfast included in the price? One more thing, do you have a room with an ocean view? And finally, is there free parking at the hotel? Thank you so much.
points: Do you have … / Is … included? / How much …?

q9.q: I'm sorry, but there is a problem I need you to resolve. When you arrive at the hotel, the staff says your reservation is not in the system. Explain the situation and offer two or three alternatives to solve the problem.
q9.ja: 롤플레이: 예약이 안 되어 있다는 문제를 설명하고 해결책 2~3가지 제안하기
model: Hi, I booked a double room for two nights last week, but you're saying my reservation isn't in the system. I have the confirmation email right here on my phone. Could you check again with my phone number? If there's really no record, could you give me a similar room at the same price? Or if the hotel is full, could you help me find another hotel nearby? I'd really appreciate your help.

q10.q: Have you ever had a problem with a reservation, like at a hotel or a restaurant? Tell me what happened and how you solved it.
q10.ja: 예약과 관련해 문제가 있었던 경험이 있나요?
model: Yes, it happened last year on my birthday. I booked a table at an Italian restaurant, but when we arrived, they said they had no reservation for us. I showed them the text message, and the manager apologized. They didn't have a table at that moment, so they gave us free drinks while we waited for about twenty minutes. In the end, it was fine.

q11.q: Let's talk about something different. How do people recycle in your country? Describe the recycling system.
q11.ja: 돌발 주제: 한국의 재활용 방법을 설명해 주세요.
model: In Korea, recycling is really strict. We have to separate plastic, paper, cans and glass, and food waste goes in a special bag. In my apartment, there's a recycling area, and we can take things out only on certain days of the week. If you don't separate things properly, you can get a fine. It's a bit annoying, but I think it's a good system.

q12.q: How has recycling changed compared to the past? Tell me about any changes you have noticed.
model: When I was a kid, people didn't separate their trash that much. Now, everyone is much more careful. For example, these days, we have to remove the labels from plastic bottles before we throw them away. Also, a lot of cafés don't give out plastic straws anymore. I think people have become more aware of environmental problems.

q1.q: Let's start the interview now. Tell me something about yourself.
model: Hi, my name is Minjun, and I'm a university student in Seoul. I'm majoring in business, and I'm in my third year. I live with my parents and my younger sister in an apartment near the Han River. In my free time, I like listening to music and riding my bike along the river. I'm a pretty outgoing person, so I enjoy meeting new people. After I graduate, I hope to work for an international company, so I'm trying hard to improve my English.
points: 이름 → 하는 일 → 사는 곳 → 취미 → 앞으로의 목표

q2.q: In the survey, you indicated that you like watching movies. What kinds of movies do you like, and why?
model: I like action movies and also animated movies. Action movies are exciting, and they help me forget about stress. Animated movies, especially Japanese ones, have really beautiful scenes and warm stories. I usually watch movies on weekends. If a movie gets good reviews, I go to the theater, but most of the time I watch them at home.

q3.q: Describe what you usually do when you go to the movies, from the beginning to the end.
q3.ja: 영화를 보러 갈 때 보통 무엇을 하나요? 처음부터 끝까지 설명해 주세요.
model: First, I check the reviews online and book tickets with an app. I usually go with my best friend. We meet about thirty minutes early and buy popcorn and drinks. After the movie, we go to a café and talk about the story. Sometimes we disagree about the ending, and that's actually the most fun part.

q4.q: Tell me about the most memorable movie you have ever seen. What was it about, and why do you remember it?
q4.ja: 가장 기억에 남는 영화는? 왜 기억에 남나요?
model: The most memorable movie for me is a documentary about a pilot who flew around the world in a small plane. I watched it with my father when I was in high school. There were so many problems during the trip, but she never gave up. After watching it, I started to think more seriously about my dreams. That's why I still remember it.

q5.q: You said that you go to parks. Describe a park you often go to. What does it look like?
model: There's a big park near my house called Olympic Park. It has huge lawns, a lake and a lot of sculptures. In the spring, there are cherry blossoms everywhere, and in the fall, the trees turn yellow and red. There are walking trails and bike paths, and on weekends, there are sometimes concerts. It's my favorite place to relax.

q6.q: What do you usually do when you go to the park? Tell me about a typical visit.
model: Usually I go there on Sunday mornings. I walk around the lake for about an hour while listening to a podcast. Then I sit on a bench and read a book or just watch people. Sometimes I meet my friends there, and we play badminton. On the way home, I usually stop at a bakery and buy some bread.

q7.q: Tell me about a special day you had at a park. What happened?
q7.ja: 공원에서 있었던 특별한 하루를 말해 주세요.
model: Last spring, my family had a picnic in the park to celebrate my grandmother's seventieth birthday. We prepared lots of food, and my sister and I made a cake. While we were eating, a street musician started playing near us, and he even played a birthday song for my grandmother. She was so happy that she cried a little. I'll never forget that day.

q8.q: Let me give you a situation to act out. You want to buy a new smartphone. Go to an electronics store and ask the clerk three or four questions about the phone you want.
model: Hi, I'm looking for a new smartphone. I'm interested in this model. How long does the battery last? And how much storage does it have? Also, does it come in other colors, like blue or green? Lastly, is there any discount if I trade in my old phone? Thanks for your help.
points: Is there …? / Does it …? / How long …?

q9.q: I'm sorry, but there is a problem. After you bought the phone, you found out that it doesn't charge. Call the store, explain the problem, and suggest two or three ways to solve it.
q9.ja: 롤플레이: 산 휴대폰이 충전되지 않는 문제를 설명하고 해결책 제안하기
model: Hello, I bought a smartphone at your store yesterday, but it won't charge at all. I tried a different cable and charger, but it still doesn't work. Could I exchange it for a new one? If you don't have the same model in stock, could I get a refund? Or, if you can repair it within two or three days, that would be okay too. Please let me know what's possible.

q10.q: Have you ever bought something that didn't work properly? Tell me what happened and what you did about it.
q10.ja: 산 물건이 제대로 작동하지 않았던 경험은?
model: Yes, I once bought wireless earphones online, and the right one didn't make any sound. I contacted the seller and sent a video showing the problem. They apologized and sent me a new pair, but it took almost two weeks. Since then, I prefer to buy electronics at a store, so I can exchange them right away.

q11.q: Let's talk about the weather. Describe the seasons in your country. What is the weather like in each season?
q11.ja: 돌발 주제: 한국의 계절과 날씨를 설명해 주세요.
model: Korea has four distinct seasons. Spring is warm, and flowers bloom everywhere, but there's a lot of fine dust. Summer is hot and humid, and we have a rainy season in July. Fall is my favorite season, because the sky is clear and the weather is cool. Winter is very cold and dry, and sometimes it snows.

q12.q: How has the weather in your country changed compared to when you were a child?
q12.ja: 어렸을 때와 비교해 날씨는 어떻게 바뀌었나요?
model: I think summers have become much hotter. When I was a kid, we didn't use the air conditioner that often, but now we can't live without it. Also, spring and fall feel shorter than before. It seems like it goes from winter to summer very quickly. I think climate change is the reason.
